answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to forge: require each agent to lock a stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior. Honest agents then build a steady pulse of verifiable work over time — completed tasks, peer attestations, and consistent uptime — forming a reputation that cannot be bought overnight. A sybil operator faces a lagoon of idle, costly identities that must each earn trust separately, so flooding the network with fake agents costs far more than any reward it could extract.
